title: PL-300: Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst
description: Practice exam for the PL-300 certification covering Power BI data preparation, modeling, visualization, and deployment.
domains: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data

scoring_guide.label: GOOD — Review missed domains and practice more.
NEEDS WORK — More hands-on Power BI practice recommended.

questions.text: You need to connect to a SQL Server database in Power BI Desktop and load only rows where Status = 'Active'. Where should you apply this filter for best performance?

options.text: In a DAX calculated table after loading all rows
In Power Query (M), before the data is loaded, using a filter step or native query
In a report-level filter on each visual

questions.explanation: Filtering in Power Query (query folding to the source) reduces the volume of data loaded into the model. Applying filters after load wastes memory and slows refresh.

questions.text: Which Power Query feature allows a transformation step to be pushed back to the source database as a native SQL query rather than executed locally?
questions.explanation: Query folding translates Power Query M steps into source-native queries (e.g., SQL), so the heavy lifting is done at the database rather than in Power BI.

questions.text: You have a table with a column containing values like '2024-Q1', '2024-Q2'. You need to split this into separate Year and Quarter columns. Which Power Query transform achieves this?
questions.explanation: Split Column by Delimiter (using '-' as the delimiter) creates two new columns, which you can then rename to Year and Quarter.

questions.text: You have separate Sales tables for 2022, 2023, and 2024 with identical schemas. You want to combine them into a single table. Which Power Query operation should you use?
questions.explanation: Append Queries stacks tables with the same schema on top of each other (like SQL UNION ALL). Merge is for joining tables on a key (like SQL JOIN).

questions.text: Which Power Query data profiling tool shows the distribution of unique vs. duplicate values in a column?
questions.explanation: Column distribution shows distinct and unique counts as well as a histogram of value frequency. Column quality shows valid/error/empty percentages.

questions.text: You need to configure a large Import-mode dataset to only refresh the last 12 months of data each day, while keeping historical data intact. Which Power BI feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Incremental refresh partitions the data by date range so only the recent window is refreshed each cycle, while older partitions remain untouched.

questions.text: You are importing data from an Excel workbook that has its data in a named Table (not just a sheet range). What is the recommended way to connect to it in Power BI Desktop?

options.text: Connect to the workbook and select the named Table object in Navigator
Copy-paste the data into Power BI

questions.explanation: Connecting via the Excel connector and selecting the named Table ensures structural refresh reliability and query folding compatibility for supported sources.

questions.text: A column in your source data contains a mix of numeric values and the text 'N/A'. When Power BI auto-detects the column type as Whole Number, the 'N/A' entries become errors. What is the best remediation?

options.text: Replace 'N/A' with null (or 0) in Power Query before the type change step
Keep the column as Text type
Ignore errors; they don't affect visuals

questions.explanation: Replacing 'N/A' with null before the type conversion step is the cleanest approach; the column then converts cleanly to numeric with nulls for missing values.

questions.text: You need to combine data from a SQL table and a SharePoint list based on a matching CustomerID column. Which Power Query operation should you use?

options.text: Merge Queries (using CustomerID as the join key)

questions.explanation: Merge Queries joins two tables on a shared column (like SQL JOIN). Append stacks rows from tables with the same schema.

questions.text: What does the 'Enable load' option control for a Power Query query?

options.text: Whether the query results are loaded into the data model or only used as an intermediate/reference step
Whether the query can access the internet
Whether the query runs in parallel

questions.explanation: Disabling 'Enable load' means the query acts as a staging/helper query — its output is available for other queries but does not add a table to the data model.

questions.text: In a star schema, a Fact table contains a SalesAmount column and foreign keys to Date, Customer, and Product dimension tables. Where should you define a 'Total Sales' measure?

options.text: B or C — both are common and valid

questions.explanation: Measures can live in any table; placing them in the fact table is logical, while a dedicated hidden 'Measures' table keeps things organised. Both are widely accepted patterns.

questions.text: Which DAX function returns the sum of an expression evaluated for each row in a table, ignoring current filter context on a specific column?
questions.explanation: CALCULATE with ALL() removes filters from specified columns, allowing a measure to compute totals unaffected by slicer/visual context on those columns.

questions.text: You have a Sales table and want to show each product's sales as a percentage of the total across all products, regardless of which product is selected in a slicer. Which DAX pattern achieves this?
questions.explanation: DIVIDE with ALL(Product) in CALCULATE removes the product filter to get the grand total denominator, yielding each product's share of total.

questions.text: What is the correct relationship direction to set between a Date dimension table and a Sales fact table to enable standard time intelligence calculations?

options.text: One-to-many from Date to Sales, single direction (Date filters Sales)
Many-to-one from Date to Sales, bidirectional

questions.explanation: The standard star-schema pattern is one-to-many from the dimension (Date) to the fact (Sales), with a single-direction filter. Bidirectional is only needed in specific snowflake/bridge scenarios.

questions.text: You need a DAX measure that returns sales for the same period in the previous year. Which function is most direct?
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the current date filter back exactly one year, making it the most readable choice for year-over-year comparisons.

questions.text: What is the key difference between a calculated column and a measure in DAX?

options.text: Calculated columns are evaluated at query time; measures are computed at refresh time
Calculated columns are computed row-by-row at refresh and stored in the model; measures are evaluated dynamically at query time in filter context

questions.explanation: Calculated columns add a stored column to the table (consuming memory), while measures are computed on the fly and respond to filter context — making measures more flexible and memory-efficient for aggregations.

questions.text: You need to look up the Category name from a Product dimension table for each row in a Sales calculated column. Which DAX function should you use?
questions.explanation: RELATED traverses an existing model relationship to retrieve a value from the 'one' side (Product) from the 'many' side (Sales). LOOKUPVALUE works without a relationship.

questions.text: Which storage mode allows some tables to operate in Import and others in DirectQuery within the same Power BI model?
questions.explanation: A Composite model combines Import-cached tables with DirectQuery tables in the same model, offering flexibility between performance and real-time freshness.

questions.text: You want to enforce that Sales Manager A can only see data for Region = 'North' when they open the report. Which Power BI feature should you implement?

options.text: Row-level security (RLS) with a DAX filter on the Region column

questions.explanation: RLS filters rows via a DAX expression tied to user identity (e.g., USERPRINCIPALNAME()), so each user only sees their permitted rows.

questions.text: What does the USERELATIONSHIP function do in DAX?

options.text: Creates a new relationship at report run-time
Activates an inactive relationship for the duration of a CALCULATE expression
Returns all values from the related table

questions.explanation: USERELATIONSHIP temporarily activates an inactive relationship within a CALCULATE call, enabling role-playing dimension patterns (e.g., a Date table used for both OrderDate and ShipDate).

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: A report page shows a bar chart filtered to 'North' region. A user clicks a bar representing Product A. What Power BI interaction automatically highlights the related data in other visuals on the page?
questions.explanation: Clicking a data point in one visual automatically cross-filters or cross-highlights other visuals on the same page — this is default Power BI interaction behavior.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: You want a button on a report page that, when clicked, navigates the user to a detail page pre-filtered by the selected product. Which feature should you use?
questions.explanation: Drillthrough allows a user to right-click (or use a button) to navigate to a detail page pre-filtered by the context of the selected data point.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: Which Power BI feature lets you save and restore a specific state of a report (filters, slicer selections, visual visibility) as a named snapshot?

options.text: A and B — both are types of bookmarks

questions.explanation: Both report bookmarks (created by the report author, shared with all viewers) and personal bookmarks (created by each viewer for themselves) save report state.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: Which chart type is best for showing the proportional contribution of each product to total sales when there are 5 products?
questions.explanation: Pie/donut charts are designed for part-to-whole relationships. With only 5 categories they remain readable; more categories make them unwieldy.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: A user needs to see a report but should not be able to edit it or access the underlying data. Which Power BI sharing method provides this?

options.text: Publish to the Power BI service and share the report link with view-only access
Export to PowerPoint and email it

questions.explanation: Publishing to the service and sharing with view access gives consumers a read-only, always-current view without exposing the .pbix or the model directly.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: Which Power BI feature allows you to add an AI-powered visual that automatically finds and displays the key influencers of a selected metric?
questions.explanation: The Key Influencers visual uses AI to identify which categorical factors most influence a selected numeric metric up or down.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: You want a slicer on Page 1 to also filter visuals on Page 2 and Page 3 of the same report. Which feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Sync slicers (View > Sync slicers) let you synchronise a slicer's selection across multiple report pages.

questions.domain: Domain 3 · Visualize and Analyze the Data
questions.text: Which visual type displays sequential increases and decreases, making it ideal for showing how individual factors build up to a total (e.g., revenue bridge)?
questions.explanation: A waterfall chart shows incremental positive/negative contributions to a total — ideal for P&L bridges, revenue waterfalls, etc.

questions.text: You want to promote a Power BI report from a Development workspace to a Production workspace while maintaining a separation of environments. Which Power BI feature is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines automate promotion of Power BI content (reports, datasets, dashboards) across Development, Test, and Production stages.

questions.text: You publish a Power BI report to the service. The underlying dataset is in Import mode and pulls from an on-premises SQL Server. What must you configure for scheduled refresh to work?

options.text: An on-premises data gateway and valid data source credentials in the dataset settings
A VPN connection on the Power BI gateway

questions.explanation: An on-premises gateway acts as a bridge between the Power BI cloud service and on-premises data. Valid credentials must also be configured in the dataset settings.

questions.text: What is a Power BI app, and how does it differ from a workspace?

options.text: A Power BI app is a bundled, published collection of dashboards and reports shared with a broad audience; a workspace is the collaborative authoring environment
Apps are only available in Premium capacity
Workspaces can be shared externally; apps cannot

questions.explanation: An App packages selected content from a workspace into a curated, versioned distribution for consumers. The workspace is where authors build and collaborate.

questions.text: Which endorsement level requires a Fabric/Power BI admin to grant approval and indicates the highest level of organizational trust for a dataset or report?
questions.explanation: Certified endorsement requires tenant admin enablement and a designated certifier; it signals the item meets organizational data quality/governance standards. Promoted can be set by any owner.

questions.text: You need to allow an external guest user (outside your organization) to view a Power BI report. What must be enabled?

options.text: Azure Active Directory B2B (external sharing) must be enabled by admin, and the guest must be invited
Export to PDF and email it

questions.explanation: External sharing uses Azure AD B2B. The Power BI admin must enable external sharing, and the guest user must be added to the tenant as a B2B guest.

questions.text: What does the Power BI Usage Metrics report show?

options.text: Who has viewed a report or dashboard, how many times, and from what platform

questions.explanation: Usage Metrics tracks consumer engagement: view counts, unique viewers, and access methods — helping authors understand report adoption.

questions.text: You need to ensure that a dataset used by 20 reports is refreshed nightly and that all 20 reports always reflect the latest data without each having its own connection. Which pattern should you use?

options.text: Embed the same data in all 20 .pbix files
Publish a shared (certified) dataset to the service; connect all 20 reports to it via Live Connection

questions.explanation: A shared published dataset (the 'single source of truth' pattern) means all 20 reports connect live to one refreshed dataset — maximising consistency and minimizing duplication.

questions.text: Which Power BI sensitivity label action helps prevent users from accidentally saving confidential report data to an unprotected location?

options.text: Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) sensitivity labels that apply encryption and access controls to exports

questions.explanation: MIP sensitivity labels (set in Power BI and propagated via Microsoft Purview) can enforce encryption, access restrictions, and usage rules when data is exported to Excel, PDF, etc.
